sources.researchNote: The printed caption reads: “At the Beachcomber on opening night was Hoagy Carmichael, center. Here he is chatting with a fellow songwriter Sidney Clare, left, and Arthur Gordon, of Fleishman Distilleries.” The identification of Clare as a songwriter distinguishes him from namesakes. The photograph documents him in Palm Springs later in life, at the Beachcomber opening rather than a professional gathering.

media.title: Sidney Clare with Hoagy Carmichael at the Beachcomber — Desert Sun, 1956
media.description: Press photograph from the opening night of the Beachcomber in Palm Springs, published in the Desert Sun on 13 October 1956: Sidney Clare at the left, Hoagy Carmichael in the centre and Arthur Gordon of Fleischmann Distilleries at the right. The printed caption is reproduced beneath the picture.
media.altText: Three men in suits standing in conversation at a bar opening, with the newspaper caption printed beneath.
media.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared, and the inventory usually relied on for this question does not reach it. The picture is credited to the newspaper itself, and a United States issue of 1956 kept its copyright only if it carried a notice and the registration was renewed in its twenty-eighth year, in 1984. The University of Pennsylvania inventory of first periodical renewals has no entry for the title, but it says of itself that it is not complete for periodicals whose first renewed issue or contribution was 1950 or later, and sends the reader to the Copyright Office public records for those; a 1956 issue falls outside what it can show. A title search of those public records surfaced no newspaper or periodical of this name. The front-page flag was examined and carries no copyright notice — thirtieth year, volume XXX, number 38, fourteen pages, ten cents a copy — but a notice of the kind the 1909 Act required could stand instead in the editorial-page masthead, which has not been seen. The California Digital Newspaper Collection states a position of its own, and it is restrictive: its terms make the digital content available for personal use and not for copying, re-use or incorporation into any database without the written permission of the Center for Bibliographical Studies and Research at the University of California, Riverside. That condition is about the scan, not about the newspaper page it reproduces. The local 331 × 238 pixel reproduction is used for the identification of the sitter alone.
media.publicCaption: Sidney Clare (left), co-composer of “Miss Annabelle Lee”, which Kaper arranged as a two-piano novelty and recorded with Hermann Bick, with Hoagy Carmichael (centre) and Arthur Gordon at the Beachcomber. Printed in the Desert Sun on 13 October 1956.
